topic: Fixed-income market segments, issuers, and investors
stem:
Consider the following:
I. BBB-
II. BB+
III. B
How many of the above S&P credit ratings are considered investment grade by market participants?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

A is correct. The investment-grade line in the module is BBB- or higher. Item I, BBB-, sits exactly on that line, so it qualifies. Item II, BB+, is just below the line and is speculative grade. Item III, B, is also below the line. One item qualifies, so the answer is Only one.

Option B is incorrect. Only two would require one more rating besides BBB- to be investment grade, but BB+ is specifically the highest speculative-grade rating.

Option C is incorrect. All three cannot qualify because both BB+ and B are below investment grade.

topic: Fixed-income market segments, issuers, and investors
stem:
Consider the following:
I. New issuers for which investors are more likely to require collateral because operating cash flows are less stable
II. Formerly investment-grade issuers whose credit quality has deteriorated since issuance
III. Developed market sovereign issuers that investors often treat as default risk free
How many of the above are described as high-yield issuers or part of the high-yield category?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

B is correct. The module places two types of issuers in the high-yield category here. Item I qualifies because new issuers with less stable cash flows may need collateral and are high-yield-type borrowers. Item II qualifies because fallen angels are formerly investment-grade issuers whose credit quality has deteriorated. Item III does not qualify because developed market sovereign issuers are generally the most creditworthy borrowers in their markets. Two items qualify, so the answer is Only two.

Option A is incorrect. Only one would ignore either the new less stable issuer or the fallen angel, both of which the module associates with high yield.

Option C is incorrect. All three would incorrectly classify developed market sovereign issuers as high yield.

topic: Fixed-income market segments, issuers, and investors
stem:
Consider the following:
I. Near-term obligations and liquid cash alternatives are often met with money market securities
II. Pension funds and insurance companies may favor maturity profiles that match long-term liabilities
III. Investors may take credit risk at any point on the maturity spectrum to augment returns
How many of the above statements are consistent with fixed-income investor positions in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

C is correct. The module says investors position along maturity and credit spectra. Item I qualifies because near-term obligations and liquid cash alternatives are often met with money market securities. Item II qualifies because pension funds and insurers may match long-term liabilities with suitable maturity profiles. Item III qualifies because investors may take credit risk at any maturity to increase expected return. Three items qualify, so the answer is All the three.

Option A is incorrect. Only one is too low because the module supports each of the three investor-positioning statements.

Option B is incorrect. Only two is also too low because none of the listed statements contradicts the module.

topic: Fixed-income market segments, issuers, and investors
stem:
Consider the following:
I. Treasury bills
II. Leveraged loans
III. Mortgage-backed securities
How many of the above appear in the module's long-term default-risk-free issuer category?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

A is correct. The default-risk-free category in the module is tied to Treasury instruments from highly creditworthy sovereign issuers. Item I, Treasury bills, qualifies as a Treasury instrument even though it is short term. Item II, leveraged loans, appears in the high-yield area. Item III, mortgage-backed securities, appears under investment-grade long-term instruments, not default-risk-free. One item qualifies, so the answer is Only one.

Option B is incorrect. Only two would require either leveraged loans or mortgage-backed securities to be default-risk-free, but the module places them in other credit categories.

Option C is incorrect. All three fails because leveraged loans and mortgage-backed securities are not in the default-risk-free category.

topic: Fixed-income market segments, issuers, and investors
stem:
Consider the following:
I. Probability of default
II. Expected loss under a default scenario
III. Issuer common stock dividend history
How many of the above are part of the credit rating assessment described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

B is correct. The module says credit ratings measure the ability to meet debt obligations using both probability of default and expected loss if default occurs. Item I qualifies because probability of default is named. Item II qualifies because expected loss under default is named. Item III does not qualify because common stock dividend history is not part of that definition. Two items qualify, so the answer is Only two.

Option A is incorrect. Only one misses that the rating idea has two named parts: likelihood of default and loss if default happens.

Option C is incorrect. All three incorrectly adds an equity dividend fact that the module does not use in the credit rating definition.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. A single issuer may have many individual fixed-income securities outstanding
II. Fixed-income indexes have less constituent turnover than equity indexes
III. Fixed-income index constituents are usually equally weighted
How many of the above are differences between fixed-income and equity indexes described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

A is correct. The module gives specific bond-index differences. Item I qualifies because one issuer can have many bonds outstanding, which increases index constituents. Item II does not qualify because fixed-income indexes have more, not less, turnover than equity indexes. Item III does not qualify because bond indexes are usually weighted by market value of debt outstanding, not equally weighted. One item qualifies, so the answer is Only one.

Option B is incorrect. Only two would require either lower turnover or equal weighting to be true, but both reverse the module's description.

Option C is incorrect. All three is impossible because two statements are direct opposites of the module.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. A bond falls below a minimum maturity
II. A new issue meets eligibility requirements and pricing information is available
III. A bond's issuer changes its common stock voting policy
How many of the above are reasons for fixed-income index constituent changes described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

B is correct. Bond index turnover comes from rule-based additions and removals. Item I qualifies because bonds are removed when they fall below minimum maturity. Item II qualifies because new eligible issues can be added when required information and pricing are available. Item III does not qualify because common stock voting policy is not a bond index inclusion rule. Two items qualify, so the answer is Only two.

Option A is incorrect. Only one sees only one side of rebalancing, but the module includes both removals and additions.

Option C is incorrect. All three incorrectly treats an equity governance fact as a fixed-income index rule.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. High-yield debt instruments
II. Investment-grade fixed-coupon capital market securities that meet the minimum issuance size
III. Senior and subordinated issues that otherwise meet the index criteria
How many of the above are excluded from the Bloomberg Barclays Global Aggregate Index as described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

A is correct. For the Global Aggregate Index, the module excludes high-yield and unrated debt and instruments below minimum size. Item I qualifies as excluded because it is high yield. Item II does not qualify as excluded because investment-grade fixed-coupon securities that meet size rules may be included. Item III does not qualify as excluded because senior and subordinated issues are eligible if they meet the other rules. One item qualifies, so the answer is Only one.

Option B is incorrect. Only two would wrongly exclude one of the eligible categories described by the index rules.

Option C is incorrect. All three is wrong because the module allows qualifying investment-grade fixed-coupon bonds and qualifying senior or subordinated issues.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. The index uses only US dollar-denominated bonds
II. Bonds with coupon or redemption payments linked to an exchange rate are not eligible
III. Rebalancing occurs on the final US business day of each month
How many of the above are features of the J.P. Morgan EMBI+ Index described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

C is correct. The EMBI+ rules in the module are narrow and specific. Item I qualifies because the index includes only US dollar-denominated bonds. Item II qualifies because bonds with coupon or redemption payments linked to an exchange rate are not eligible. Item III qualifies because rebalancing occurs on the final US business day of each month. Three items qualify, so the answer is All the three.

Option A is incorrect. Only one is too low because all three features are stated in the EMBI+ description.

Option B is incorrect. Only two is too low because none of the three listed features conflicts with the module.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. Minimum MSCI ESG rating of BBB or higher
II. Exclusion of issuers with a Red MSCI Controversies score
III. Inclusion of fixed-rate perpetual bonds
How many of the above are eligibility features of the Bloomberg Barclays MSCI Euro Corporate Sustainable SRI Index?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

B is correct. The Euro Corporate Sustainable SRI Index uses both normal bond filters and ESG filters. Item I qualifies because the index requires an MSCI ESG rating of BBB or higher. Item II qualifies because issuers with a Red MSCI Controversies score are excluded. Item III does not qualify because fixed-rate perpetual bonds are excluded, not included. Two items qualify, so the answer is Only two.

Option A is incorrect. Only one misses that the ESG rating rule and the controversies exclusion are both part of the index rules.

Option C is incorrect. All three incorrectly turns an explicit exclusion of fixed-rate perpetual bonds into an inclusion feature.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. An issuer sells a new bond to raise capital
II. Existing bonds are traded among investors
III. A national treasury sells sovereign debt through a public auction
How many of the above describe primary fixed-income market activity?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

B is correct. Primary market activity means the issuer is raising financing by selling new debt. Item I qualifies because the issuer sells a new bond to raise capital. Item II does not qualify because existing bonds traded among investors are secondary market trades. Item III qualifies because sovereign debt issuance usually occurs through a public auction led by the treasury or finance ministry. Two items qualify, so the answer is Only two.

Option A is incorrect. Only one misses that sovereign public auctions are also primary issuance.

Option C is incorrect. All three incorrectly counts secondary trading of existing bonds as primary market activity.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. New corporate legal entities formed after a merger, acquisition, or divestiture that refinance existing debt
II. Companies with more predictable cash flows that begin issuing debt at a mature life-cycle stage
III. Sovereign governments raising external foreign currency debt for the first time
How many of the above are examples of debut bond issuers described in the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

C is correct. A debut issuer is an issuer coming to the bond market for the first time. Item I qualifies because the module lists new corporate legal entities after mergers, acquisitions, or divestitures that refinance debt. Item II qualifies because mature companies with more predictable cash flows may begin issuing debt. Item III qualifies because sovereign governments may raise external foreign currency debt for the first time. Three items qualify, so the answer is All the three.

Option A is incorrect. Only one ignores two other first-time bond issuer examples stated in the module.

Option B is incorrect. Only two is still too low because all three listed cases are debut issuer examples.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. The intermediary guarantees the sale of the bond issue at an offering price negotiated with the issuer
II. The intermediary tries to sell the issue on a commission basis only if it can do so
III. The intermediary removes the bond from trading when the issuer's equity is delisted
How many of the above describe an underwritten bond offering?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

A is correct. An underwritten offering is defined by the underwriter guaranteeing the sale at the negotiated offering price. Item I qualifies because it states that guarantee. Item II does not qualify because selling on commission only if possible is a best-efforts offering. Item III does not qualify because equity delisting is unrelated to primary bond underwriting. One item qualifies, so the answer is Only one.

Option B is incorrect. Only two would confuse best efforts with underwriting, but best efforts lacks the sale guarantee.

Option C is incorrect. All three wrongly includes a secondary-market distress fact and a best-efforts fact as underwriting features.

stem:
Consider the following:
I. On-the-run developed market sovereign bonds usually have bid-offer spreads equal to a fraction of a basis point
II. Recently issued higher-credit-quality corporate bonds from frequent issuers usually have tighter bid-offer spreads than more seasoned bonds
III. Less frequent corporate issuers or seasoned bonds of frequent issuers may have bid-offer spreads of at least 10-20 basis points or more for small sizes
How many of the above liquidity statements are consistent with the module?
explanation:
First Principles Thinking: classification rule

C is correct. Liquidity in the module is read through bid-offer spreads: tighter spreads mean more liquidity, wider spreads mean less liquidity. Item I qualifies because on-the-run developed market sovereign bonds can have spreads equal to a fraction of a basis point. Item II qualifies because recently issued higher-quality corporate bonds from frequent issuers usually have the greatest corporate liquidity. Item III qualifies because less frequent or seasoned corporate bonds may have spreads of at least 10-20 basis points or more for small sizes. Three items qualify, so the answer is All the three.

Option A is incorrect. Only one is too low because each statement matches a different liquidity tier in the module.

Option B is incorrect. Only two is too low because none of the three listed liquidity statements is inconsistent with the module.
